newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ELKINGTON HOLDS ON TO ONE-STROKE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELKINGTON HOLDS ON TO ONE-STROKE LEAD.

text.p: Steve
Elkington of Australia held on to a one-shot lead at the
Players Championship with a three under par 69 at the TPC at
Sawgrass on Friday.
In second place at eight under was Larry Mize, who has had
two rounds of 68. In third place a stroke further back was
Tommy Tolles, a runner-up here last year, who shot a 67, and
David Edwards, in with a 70.
Tolles finished his round with an eagle on the 16th hole,
and birdies on 17 and 18.
Four players were tied in fifth place at six under,
including 1992 Players winner Davis Love, whose round of 66,
the day's low, included a double bogey.
Also at six under were Tom Lehman, who had a 71,
Australian Craig Parry, with a 67, and Brian Watts, an
American who plays the Japanese tour, who shot a 68.
"At this tournament, you need to make as many birdies as
you can, because you know you're going to need them later on,"
said Elkington.
Elkington, who won this tournament in 1991, had five
birdies and two bogeys in his round.
"Had a couple of loose shots on the back nine, but other
than that I played steady," said Elkington of the two poor
drives which resulted in bogeys on the 10th and 15th holes.
Tiger Woods shot a two-over-par 73 and finished at even
par.
The cut came at two over par 146.
